meta.name: EN 16931 e-Invoice Lint
meta.basis: EN 16931-1:2017+A1:2019 core invoice model and national CIUS

core_terms.msg: BT-1 invoice number is not mapped. EN 16931 makes it mandatory; a receiver's ERP rejects the document before a human ever sees it.
BT-2 issue date is not mapped. It is the date the VAT liability is pinned to, so no tax engine can post the document without it.
BT-5 invoice currency code is not mapped. EN 16931 has no default currency; the amounts below are meaningless without it.
BT-24 specification identifier (CustomizationID) is missing. Without it the receiver cannot tell which CIUS to validate against — here that would be {cius}.
BT-23 business process type (ProfileID) is missing. Peppol access points route on this field; most will still accept the invoice, some will not.
BT-31 seller VAT identifier is not mapped. For a domestic B2B invoice in {country} this is mandatory and is the key the tax authority matches on.
BT-48 buyer VAT identifier is not mapped. It is conditional in EN 16931 but required for reverse charge and for intra-Community supplies.
BT-49 buyer electronic address is not mapped. This is the routing address of the invoice; without it there is nowhere to deliver the document in {cius}.
BG-23 VAT breakdown group is missing. EN 16931 requires one subtotal per VAT category and rate, not a single tax figure.
BT-112 invoice total with VAT is not mapped. BR-CO-15 checks it against the sum of BT-109 and BT-110, so the document fails schematron validation.
BT-115 amount due for payment is not mapped. It is what the buyer actually pays after prepaid amounts and rounding.

core_terms.check: BT-9 due date or BT-20 terms
core_terms.msg: Neither BT-9 payment due date nor BT-20 payment terms is mapped. BR-CO-25 requires one of the two, so this is a validation error at the receiver.
BT-30 seller legal registration identifier is missing. Public buyers in {country} routinely reject invoices that carry no commercial-register or equivalent id.
BG-25 invoice lines are not mapped. A document with totals but no lines is invoice data, not an invoice, under EN 16931.

country_terms.msg: BT-10 buyer reference is missing. In {cius} the Leitweg-ID is mandatory and the receiving platform rejects the invoice outright.
No SIREN or SIRET is mapped. French B2B e-invoicing identifies both parties by SIREN (scheme 0009); a VAT number alone will not route through the PPF.
Codice Destinatario (or a PEC address) is missing. SdI has no way to deliver the FatturaPA file and will return a scarto notice.
The NIP of seller and buyer is not mapped. KSeF keys every document on NIP; without it the invoice cannot be registered and gets no KSeF number.
No Belgian enterprise number (Peppol scheme 0208) is mapped. It is the expected participant identifier for {cius}.

invoice_defects.msg: A zero or exempt VAT category is used with no BT-120 exemption reason text and no BT-121 VATEX code. BR-E/BR-AE reject the invoice; the buyer's input VAT claim dies with it.
An electronic address is mapped without its scheme identifier (EAS code). The same string means a different participant under 0088, 0204 or 0009, so routing is undefined.
The specification identifier still points at an XRechnung 1.x/2.x CIUS. XRechnung 3.0 is the version in force; 2.x identifiers are refused by the German receiving platforms.
EN 16931 syntax binding is UBL 2.1 (or CII D16B). A UBL 2.0 namespace will not validate against the EN 16931 schematron.
A monetary amount carries more than two decimals. EN 16931 fixes document-level amounts at two decimals, and BR-CO-15 arithmetic is checked on the rounded values.
A CII date is declared as format 102 but written as YYYY-MM-DD. Format 102 is YYYYMMDD with no separators.

date_rules.msg_live: The Factur-X MINIMUM/BASIC WL profile carries no line data and is not an EN 16931-compliant invoice. {country} has required compliant issuing since {date} under {statute} — that was {days_since} days ago.
date_rules.msg_before: The Factur-X MINIMUM/BASIC WL profile carries no line data and is not an EN 16931-compliant invoice. {country} starts requiring compliant issuing on {date} under {statute} — {days_left} days from {today}.

date_rules.msg_live: A PDF/e-mail fallback is still switched on. Since {date} a PDF is not an e-invoice for {country} under {statute}; a buyer who accepts this one has no deductible document.
date_rules.msg_before: A PDF/e-mail fallback is switched on. From {date} a PDF stops being an e-invoice for {country} under {statute} — {days_left} days from {today}.

date_rules.msg: The mandate date hardcoded here is {found}. For {country} the issuing obligation starts {date} under {statute} — shipping the wrong date means the switch flips on the wrong day.
No country or CIUS marker is present, so no national rule set can be applied. EN 16931 is a core invoice model; every member state adds mandatory fields on top of it.
